items.title: Dow Jones Futures Fall After Soaring Yields Hit Stocks, But Palantir Flashes Buy Signal; Trump-Xi On Tap
items.summary: The stock market fell as Treasury yields skyrocketed and oil prices rose, but Palantir and Palo Alto flashed buy signals.

items.title: Datadog (DDOG) Gains As Market Dips: What You Should Know
items.summary: In the closing of the recent trading day, Datadog (DDOG) stood at $251.49, denoting a +1.62% move from the preceding trading day.

items.title: Trump Downplayed AI Safety Concerns, but His Investment Portfolio Bought Cybersecurity Stocks
items.summary: President Donald Trump has called artificial-intelligence safety fears a “hoax.”  The president’s latest financial disclosure for July shows his portfolio bought stocks of cybersecurity companies, which address the growing need for protection as AI keeps developing.  Both the White House and the Trump Organization said Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions.

items.title: Fastly Just Ripped 138% This Year but It’s Now Falling. Is It Time to Sell?
items.summary: Fastly just turned a monster year-to-date run into a two-day slide that started at its own Investor Day, and now holders sitting on triple-digit gains face a decision that pure momentum investing was never designed to answer.

items.title: Fortinet vs. Datadog: Which Cloud Security Stock Has Better Potential?
items.summary: FTNT pairs faster billings growth, robust cash flow and a lower valuation, while DDOG delivers stronger revenue growth but faces near-term customer pressure.

items.title: Twilio, Datadog, Unity, Zscaler, and Elastic Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
items.summary: A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after falling Treasury yields eased pressure on software stocks as signs of cooler U.S.–China tensions lifted risk appetite.

items.title: Fastly Soars 14% on AI Firewall Launch; Cloudflare Climbs 7%, Datadog Rises 5%
items.summary: Fastly launched new AI traffic controls this morning and the whole edge security category moved with it, including rivals that announced nothing at all. The question buyers are not asking loudly enough is whether availability and adoption are the same thing.

items.title: 1 S&P 500 Stock for Long-Term Investors and 2 We Find Risky
items.summary: While the S&P 500 (^GSPC) includes industry leaders, not every stock in the index is a winner. Some companies are past their prime, weighed down by poor execution, weak financials, or structural headwinds.
